policy: Facts require the exact cited source; original papers, monographs, curated accounts and field guides are not interchangeable.

facts.label: Facial field marks
facts.text: Prominent blue fleshy eye wattles, purple crown, grey nuchal collar and lilac underparts are described in the attributed field guide.
facts.source: BirdForum Opus, Visayan Broadbill identification account
facts.studyScope: Field-guide summary. Use multiple characters; not a diagnostic original species description.

facts.label: Original morphological diagnosis
facts.text: The published diagnosis combines small body size, weak or absent dark tympanic marking, a narrow or absent canthal stripe, dark-bordered dorsal spots and black eyes with a blue scleral arc.
facts.source: Brown, Siler, Diesmos & Alcala (2010), Herpetological Monographs 23
facts.studyScope: Character combination from examined specimens; calls and population variation need original paper for complete identification.

facts.label: Comparative colour pattern
facts.text: Published phylogenetic comparison describes Batanes specimens as often yellow or grey and lacking the green pigment typical of many Philippine Trimeresurus flavomaculatus.
facts.source: Sanders et al. (2004), Journal of Evolutionary Biology
facts.studyScope: Diagnostic context is lineage-specific; do not identify a snake from colour alone.

facts.label: Adult coat and antlers
facts.text: Adult Visayan spotted deer retain pale body spots on a dark-brown coat; published mammal monograph describes three-tined male antlers.
facts.source: Handbook of the Mammals of the World, Rusa alfredi account (Plazi)
facts.studyScope: Adult descriptive characters; male antlers are not applicable to females or juveniles.

facts.label: Feeding and activity
facts.text: The published species monograph describes consumption of leaves, buds, young grasses and fruits, with mainly nocturnal activity.
facts.source: Handbook of the Mammals of the World, Rusa alfredi account (Plazi)
facts.studyScope: Species-level account, not a quantified diet from a named monitoring site.

facts.label: Dated IUCN global assessment
facts.text: IUCN assessed this species as Endangered in March 2016 with a decreasing population trend; this is a dated global assessment, not Philippine DENR status.
facts.source: Brook (2016), IUCN Red List, Rusa alfredi
facts.studyScope: Historical 2016 global category; do not present as a newly reassessed national legal status.

facts.label: Published physical account
facts.text: An attributed mammal account describes a small flying fox with mostly brown, sometimes grey fur and adult mass of about 145–200 g.
facts.source: Animal Diversity Web, Pteropus pumilus species account
facts.studyScope: Secondary species account; body size alone does not separate all similar flying foxes.

facts.label: Roost sociality
facts.text: The attributed species account describes small-group tree roosts rather than the very large aggregations of some other Pteropus.
facts.source: Animal Diversity Web, Pteropus pumilus species account
facts.studyScope: Source-level summary; roost size varies and is not a verified Philippine colony count.

facts.label: Adult plumage
facts.text: The attributed photographed species account records a red breast patch, green upperparts and head, and a white throat.
facts.source: John C. Avise, Avise's Birds of the World, Gallicolumba crinigera
facts.studyScope: Plumage notes from source images. Photographs are linked only, not redistributed.

facts.label: Foraging behaviour
facts.text: The attributed species captions describe a secretive, ground-feeding forest dove.
facts.source: John C. Avise, Avise's Birds of the World, Gallicolumba crinigera
facts.studyScope: Qualitative behaviour observation, not a measured feeding-rate study.

facts.label: Basic plumage
facts.text: The attributed field account describes conspicuous contrasting black-and-white plumage.
facts.studyScope: Introductory field mark only. Not a stand-alone differentiation from Ceyx flumenicola.

facts.label: Forested streams
facts.text: BirdLife's species account associates the kingfisher with forested streams and ponds, with records from some secondary and selectively logged forest.
facts.source: BirdLife DataZone, Ceyx argentatus species factsheet
facts.studyScope: Species-level habitat statements; not evidence of occurrence at any selected site.

facts.label: IUCN category (2022)
facts.text: BirdLife lists the 2022 IUCN global assessment as Near Threatened with a suspected decreasing population trend.
facts.source: BirdLife DataZone, Ceyx argentatus species factsheet
facts.studyScope: Dated global IUCN category. Keep distinct from the Philippine DENR list.

facts.label: Comparative coat pattern
facts.text: A peer-reviewed Axis identification key separates Calamian deer from the spotted chital by the absence of a distinct white-spotted coat pattern.
facts.source: Mammalian Species (2021), Axis axis comparative identification key
facts.studyScope: Comparative genus key; geographic range and other features still require corroboration.

facts.label: Forearm and cranial features
facts.text: A cited mammal account gives an 82–92 mm forearm and describes strongly forward-inclined incisors and canines with specialized extra tooth cusps.
facts.source: Animal Diversity Web, Harpyionycteris whiteheadi species account
facts.sourceLocation: Physical Description; cites Ingle and Heaney 1992
facts.studyScope: Secondary compilation from published morphology; not an independently remeasured specimen.

facts.label: Forest habitat account
facts.text: The published-attributed account describes forest dependence, with many mid-elevation records, but acknowledges captures outside that usual elevation band.
facts.source: Animal Diversity Web, Harpyionycteris whiteheadi species account
facts.studyScope: General ecology account; not a site-specific elevation limit.
